title: Active Record Query Interface — Quick Revision

sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: The N+1 query problem is the single most asked Rails production question, and this page owns it. N+1 happens when code loads a collection then lazily loads an association for each record — producing N+1 database round trips. The fix is eager loading, but which method to use depends on the SQL shape: includes auto-chooses between a separate query (preload) and a LEFT OUTER JOIN (eager_load); eager_load forces the JOIN and is required when the WHERE clause references the association; preload forces separate queries and works better for large result sets where the JOIN would produce too many rows. This page covers the full decision tree, Arel for programmatic query construction, batch processing with find_each and in_batches, and the scenario questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: n-plus-one, includes-preload-eager-load, arel-complex-queries, batch-processing. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
